landing.header: There Are Many Ways to Electrify
landing.headerDescription: Please register or sign in, then you will be prompted to tell us more about your specific requirements so we can recommend the appropriate equipment for your needs, identify incentives, and estimate cost savings. We can help with:
landing.fleetMessage: Compare the total costs of fleets of electrifying your fleet. See a quick example of a fossil fuel to electric fleet comparison by clicking “Continue as Guest” below.
landing.workplaceMessage: Discover how much it costs to install chargers at your workplace.
landing.publicMessage: Compare the costs and revenue of providing public chargers.
landing.MUDMessage: Find out how much it costs to install chargers at multi-unit dwellings (MUD).
landing.alertMessage: Looking to replace your existing Fossil Fuel Fleet? See how much you can save by electrifying your fossil fuel fleet, available as a guest user

projectType.title: How Do You Want to Electrify?
projectType.subMessage: Choose a scenario and click Next to continue.

default.subMessage: We use this information to calculate fuel costs and applicable incentives.
default.organizationTypeTooltip: Your selection from this list will be used to determine incentive eligibility
default.projectLifetimeTooltip: Project lifetime is the amount of time you plan to operate the vehicles and/or charging infrastructure. This value is used to calculate your TCO analysis over the life of the project.
default.zipcodeTooltip: The zip or postal code of your project will be used to determine electricity pricing and potentially identify incentives.
default.justice40CommunityMessage: A Justice40 community, defined by President Biden's Executive Order 14008, is prioritized to receive at least 40% of benefits from federal investments targeting climate change and environmental justice. See community definition, and map data.
default.dacMessage: Zip code includes a disadvantaged community, eligible for additional state incentives. Check the box to indicate your site is within a disadvantaged community. Disadvantaged Community Qualifications
default.alertMessage: Increased incentive amounts provided for Justice 40 Community may vary by program and eligibility.

default.subMessage: Select your first vehicle. If you select a Fossil Fuel vehicle, an EV replacement will be selected for you. You can choose to remove EV chargers from your analysis if they are not relevant to your scenario. If you do not want to include vehicles in your comparison, please create a new project and select a different project type.
default.alertMessage: If operating multiple vehicles over varying distances, consider grouping them into separate sets. You can create additional sets at the end of this setup wizard by clicking Create Scenario.
default.financeTooltip: The finance type represents how you will pay for the vehicles selected. This finance type will assume default values based on your selection to calculate the finance costs. These can be changed later in the Financing tab.

default.subMessage: This information helps us determine EV and charger recommendations based on your vehicle’s range and charging requirements. Please enter details for the vehicle you’re currently using or plan to purchase.
default.alertMessage: If vehicle usage exceeds 75 miles per day then your vehicles will need to be charged more than once per day (e.g. in the middle of the day). Alternatively, you may want to reduce the number of vehicles of this type on the previous screen so only vehicles used for under 75 miles per day are switched to EVs.

default.subMessage: Think ahead to when you expect to charge your new EVs. Enter each daily window of time you expect to charge your vehicles and where, and we will recommend an ideal charger.
default.alertMessage: The most expensive time to charge is during peak times (M-F 4 PM - 9 PM). To ensure the highest savings, charge during off-peak hours.
default.chargingCostsMessage: Use the checkboxes below to include or exclude charging costs such as purchase, installation, or operation. To exclude a cost, simply uncheck the corresponding box.
